description: Turn images into stamps, like the site’s Stamp Maker: "postage" (the picture on paper with perforated edges, a value like “1st” or “£1.50” and a caption), "rubber" (pressed in one ink with a double border, worn edges and a caption) or "seal" (round, inked, with your text around the ring). Rubber stamps and seals print a photo’s tones as an ink dot pattern for a dark or light surface; logos print by their shape. Transparent PNGs up to 1,400 px, saved next to the originals as name-<style>-stamp.png.

border.description: Postage: a paper margin around the picture with the caption below it. Off, the picture runs to the perforated edge.

caption.description: Postage and rubber: the caption. Seal: the text around the ring.

files.description: Image files or folders (a folder means the images in it). ~ is your home folder.

fill_surface.description: Rubber and seal: put the dark or light surface colour in the file instead of leaving it transparent.

ink.description: Rubber and seal ink colour, hex like #c23b2a.

ink_amount.description: Rubber and seal: how dark a photo prints, 10 to 80%.

output_dir.description: Folder to save results in. Default: next to each original. Originals are never overwritten.

shape.description: Postage and rubber: keep the picture’s proportions, or make the stamp 4:5 portrait or 5:4 landscape (photos cropped, logos fitted whole).

surface.description: Rubber and seal: the surface it’s printed on. Dark prints a photo’s light parts, light prints its dark parts.

tilt.description: A few degrees off straight, as if stamped by hand.

tones.description: Rubber and seal: natural reads like the photo on that surface; negative inverts it.

value.description: Postage: the value in the corner, e.g. “1st” or “£1.50”.

wear.description: Rubber and seal: gaps where the ink didn’t take, 0 (clean) to 80%.
